```{python}
#| label: prepare-data
import pathlib
import pandas as pd
import requests
import plotly.graph_objects as go

INDICATOR = "SL.UEM.1524.ZS"  # Youth unemployment, % of labour force aged 15-24 (modelled ILO estimate)
COUNTRIES = {
    "PER": "Peru",
    "CHL": "Chile",
    "COL": "Colombia",
    "MEX": "Mexico",
    "LCN": "Latin America & Caribbean",
}
DATA_FILE = pathlib.Path("data.csv")

# Downloads World Bank data the first time.
# To update it, delete data.csv and render again.
if not DATA_FILE.exists():
    url = (
        f"https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/{';'.join(COUNTRIES)}/indicator/{INDICATOR}"
        "?format=json&per_page=5000&date=2000:2030"
    )
    response = requests.get(url, timeout=60)
    response.raise_for_status()
    rows = response.json()[1]
    pd.DataFrame(
        [{"iso3": r["countryiso3code"], "year": int(r["date"]), "value": r["value"]} for r in rows]
    ).dropna().to_csv(DATA_FILE, index=False)

df = pd.read_csv(DATA_FILE)
df["country"] = df["iso3"].map(COUNTRIES)
df = df.sort_values(["iso3", "year"])

peru = df[df.iso3 == "PER"].set_index("year")["value"]
region = df[df.iso3 == "LCN"].set_index("year")["value"]
latest = int(peru.index.max())
latest_value = peru[latest]
change_2019 = latest_value - peru.get(2019, float("nan"))
gap_region = latest_value - region.get(latest, float("nan"))

def pct(x):
    return f"{x:.1f}%"

def pp(x):
    sign = "+" if x > 0 else "−" if x < 0 else ""
    return f"{sign}{abs(x):.1f} pp"
```

## Youth unemployment over time

```{python}
#| label: chart
#| fig-cap: "Youth unemployment (% of labour force aged 15 to 24)"
ACCENT = "#0B6E5E"
GREY = "#9AA6B4"

fig = go.Figure()
for iso3, name in COUNTRIES.items():
    series = df[df.iso3 == iso3]
    is_peru = iso3 == "PER"
    fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
        x=series.year, y=series.value, name=name, mode="lines",
        line=dict(color=ACCENT if is_peru else GREY, width=4 if is_peru else 1.5,
                  dash="dot" if iso3 == "LCN" else "solid"),
        hovertemplate=f"<b>{name}</b><br>%{{x}}: %{{y:.1f}}%<extra></extra>",
    ))
fig.update_layout(
    template="plotly_white",
    font=dict(family="Public Sans, sans-serif", size=14),
    paper_bgcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)", plot_bgcolor="rgba(0,0,0,0)",
    margin=dict(l=10, r=10, t=10, b=10), height=420,
    yaxis=dict(ticksuffix="%", gridcolor="rgba(128,128,128,0.2)"),
    xaxis=dict(showgrid=False),
    legend=dict(orientation="h", y=-0.15),
    hovermode="x unified",
)
fig.show()
```

```{python}
#| label: thumbnail
#| include: false
# Creates the image shown on the cards on the home page and the Data page.
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
fig_t, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 3.4), dpi=150)
for iso3 in COUNTRIES:
    s = df[df.iso3 == iso3]
    ax.plot(s.year, s.value, color=ACCENT if iso3 == "PER" else GREY,
            lw=3.5 if iso3 == "PER" else 1.2, ls=":" if iso3 == "LCN" else "-")
ax.axis("off")
fig_t.patch.set_facecolor("#E8EEF2")
fig_t.tight_layout(pad=0.6)
fig_t.savefig("thumbnail.png", facecolor=fig_t.get_facecolor())
plt.close(fig_t)
```

## What the data tell us

<!-- Write 2 or 3 paragraphs with your reading of the data: what changed, why it matters and which policies would help. -->

Unemployment is only part of the problem: in Peru, many young people who do work hold informal, low-productivity jobs. This indicator is best read alongside youth informality and the share of young people not in employment, education or training.

For a fuller analysis, see the study [Policies to improve youth labour market entry in Peru](https://ddhnb9vx8lz57.cloudfront.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/19091820/Estudio_empleabilidad_peru_2026.pdf) and the column [Más oportunidades para los jóvenes](https://elcomercio.pe/economia/opinion/trabajo-mas-oportunidades-para-los-jovenes-noticia/) (in Spanish).
